messages.content:
You are a blind semantic decoder of a natural-language crystal description. The user message is your only source of material-specific information. Understand the spatial narrative and produce a construction plan; do not guess missing independent numbers or look up a material. Return one JSON object only, without Markdown fences.
For sufficient information use:
{"status":"ok","space_group_number":integer,"hall_symbol":"Hall symbol stated in the text","lattice":[input_a,input_b,input_c,input_alpha,input_beta,input_gamma],"composition":{"Element":input_cell_atom_count},"orbits":[{"element":"Element","wyckoff":"multiplicity_and_letter","representative":[standard_fractional_x,standard_fractional_y,standard_fractional_z]}],"frame_transform":{"matrix":[[p11,p12,p13],[p21,p22,p23],[p31,p32,p33]],"origin_shift":[s1,s2,s3]},"round_digits":integer_or_null,"precision_corrections":[{"element":"Element","at":[input_fractional_x_before_correction,input_fractional_y_before_correction,input_fractional_z_before_correction],"delta":[fractional_dx,fractional_dy,fractional_dz]}]}
Lengths use angstroms, angles use degrees. The specified lattice and composition refer to the original input cell. Orbit representatives refer to the standard Hall coordinate frame. Copy the Hall symbol as a mathematical identifier rather than guessing a public-table integer number. Any equivalent representative of a declared orbit is allowed. Distinct independent orbits of the same element remain separate.
The geometry engine expands the public Hall symmetry orbits, applies q_input = inverse(P)(q_standard - s), selects images in the input cell, rounds fractional coordinates if round_digits is given, and applies precision corrections at their identified input-frame atom positions. If the text explicitly uses identical frames, supply identity P and zero shift. If no rounding is specified, use null. If no corrections are specified, use an empty array. All sites have full occupancy.
Numerical relations in the prose should be resolved into numbers in the plan. Do not silently replace the original geometry with an idealized one. For missing required information return {"status":"insufficient_information","reason":"..."}; for contradictory constraints return {"status":"conflict","reason":"..."}. Your input contains no source CIF or hidden data. Public crystallographic definitions are allowed; material-specific external retrieval is not.

The crystal is described in a nonstandard input cell with lattice parameters a = 5.95046852 Å, b = 4.91218733 Å, c = 4.77905391 Å, α = 75.74538104°, β = 53.13927448°, and γ = 51.11534448°, containing six atoms in total—two titanium and four silicon—corresponding to the declared input composition Ti₂Si₄. The underlying symmetry is that of space group Fddd (number 70, Hall symbol –F 2uv 2vw), an orthorhombic face-centered setting with inversion centers and three mutually perpendicular sets of glide and screw operations characteristic of this centrosymmetric group.

Because the supplied cell is not the conventional F-centered orthorhombic cell, a frame transformation is required to recover the standard description. Fractional coordinates in the input and standard frames are related by q_standard = P q_input + s, where the transformation matrix P has rows (approximately 0, 0.5, 0.5), (0.5, approximately 0, 0.5), and (0.5, 0.5, approximately 0), with the negligible off-diagonal residuals on the order of 10⁻¹⁶ reflecting floating-point rounding, and the origin shift s = (0.875, 0.875, 0.875). Applying this transformation maps the primitive-like input cell onto the conventional face-centered cell of Fddd, in which the full symmetry content becomes manifest.

Within the standard frame, the structure is built from two independent crystallographic orbits. Titanium occupies the Wyckoff site 8a, with the representative atom at fractional coordinates (1/8, 1/8, 1/8); the full orbit comprises eight equivalent titanium positions generated by the face-centering translations and the point symmetry of Fddd, all symmetry-equivalent to this representative with no free positional parameters. Silicon occupies the Wyckoff site 16f, a sixteen-fold general-multiplicity orbit constrained to the special form (1/8, y, 1/8), with the single free parameter y = 0.461666 (rounded to six decimal places as specified). Thus the silicon sublattice is described by one independent coordinate, with all sixteen silicon positions in the conventional cell derived from the representative (0.125, 0.461666, 0.125) through the combined action of the F-centering and the space-group operations.

The resulting three-dimensional arrangement consists of titanium atoms fixed at the high-symmetry 8a positions, interleaved with a silicon sublattice whose members lie on planes of constant fractional x = 1/8 and z = 1/8, displaced along the b direction according to the free parameter y ≈ 0.4617 and its symmetry-related values. The face-centered symmetry replicates this motif throughout the conventional cell, and the inverse of the given transformation recovers the original six-atom input cell with its reduced composition Ti₂Si₄. No positional corrections beyond the stated rounding precision are required, as the listed coordinates faithfully represent the input geometry within six decimal places.
